notes: Third sweep (2026-10-22-b) at head 0397dec: five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (the transcripts name only that model), uncommitted false and one skill_hash; each transcript contains the reworded one-step `with` paragraph ("This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step ...") and the new `do:` rule. Opus-1 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md; haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read SKILL.md only (the transcripts show no other Read of a skill file). Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all five meet it. In the scratch folder all five files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors. Doctests: opus-1 2 pass, haiku-1 2 pass, haiku-2 3 pass, sonnet-1 2 of 3 pass (line 109 fails), sonnet-2 3 pass.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The sentence added since db91c23, "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result: the `with` saves the error clause and costs the reader a search for steps that are not there." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 150), decides nothing in this batch: no run writes a one-step `with` in a public function (opus-1's public from_data/1 functions have four or five steps, and its public parse/1 uses case). The verdicts are decided by the unchanged "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." (line 118) and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (line 150). Violating runs out of 5: one-step `with` 1 (sonnet-1, twice: line 135 in parse_event("payment.succeeded", ...) and line 226 in timestamp_field/2); of those, a `case` nested in the body on a second fallible call 1 (sonnet-1 line 227 cases on DateTime.from_unix/1, the shape of the rule's second Instead-of example); large `else` 0 (no run writes a `with ... else`). Haiku-1 writes the single-step form the rule asks for, case payment_fields(data) do (lines 112 and 119). Every other `with` in the five files has two to six steps.

Not counted under the `with` rule, as in the previous sweep: a one-step `case` whose :ok branch calls another function that can fail (opus-1 Fields.currency/2 lines 207-208 and Fields.unix_time/2 line 217, sonnet-2 timestamp_field/2 line 176). The rule's sentences name a one-step `with`.

Other rules changed since db91c23 that are not in this case's list: the new `do:` rule and the captures rule (and Assert with patterns in testing.md, not exercised). Breaks of the `do:` rule are listed under other_violations: opus-1 message/1 (lines 148-155), three one-expression bodies wrapped onto a `do:` line with no guard in the head, decided by "A one-expression body too long for the head's line wants a block or a helper; a head that `mix format` wraps because of a long guard is fine as wrapped."; sonnet-1 parse_event/3, whose last clause (line 168) stays on `do:` while the other three clauses are blocks, decided by "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks." The two-clause parse/1 functions with one block and one `do:` clause (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) are not a majority of blocks and are not counted. No file has a capture with &2 or &3 or an fn.

Unchanged rules follow the previous sweeps' standard. Multi-clause heads: haiku-2 line 84, def parse(%{"type" => type} = payload) do, binds type with no guard and uses it only in the body, the shape the 2026-10-21 sweep graded violated in baseline-sonnet-1 (def parse(%{"type" => type, "data" => data} = payload) when is_map(data)); the 2026-10-22 baseline Sonnet runs were clean only because they guarded the bound type. Opus-1's ParseError.message/1 binds the reason tuple's element next to the tag that selects the clause (lines 148-155), not counted, as for the previous skill-opus-1's Error.message/1. Struct rule: opus-1's Payments.Webhook.ParseError (line 145, defexception [:reason]) has @type t but no @enforce_keys, although message/1 has no clause for a nil reason; the previous sweep's skill-opus-1 evidence counted its exception among the structs that have @enforce_keys, so this one is counted as violated. It is the only break of the struct rule in the batch and the closest call; without it opus-1 would be clean on that rule. Haiku-2's def parse(_payload) returning :invalid_payload for a map without "type" goes in checks only, as the previous sweep did for baseline-haiku-2. data["failure_reason"] (haiku-1 line 121, haiku-2 line 119) reads an optional key and is allowed. The comments in haiku-1 (lines 103-105) and haiku-2 (lines 97-98) give reasons and are clean. Sonnet-1's failing doctest (line 109, ~U[2024-09-22 09:46:40Z] for 1727000000, which is 10:13:20Z) is counted under Comments, as the previous sweep counted baseline-sonnet-2's identical timestamp. An if inside a case (haiku-1, haiku-2) and a case inside a with (sonnet-1) go under Keep functions short in other_violations, as before.

Naming: no fetch_* or get_* function in any run; lookups are named by their job (Fields.string/2, required_field/3, typed_field/3, string_field/2, amount_field/2, timestamp_field/2). Every variable named data holds the payload's "data" map. Borderline names not counted, as earlier grades did not count object, body, envelope or details: object (haiku-1, haiku-2), envelope and payment (sonnet-1), details (sonnet-2), kind (haiku-2), fields (haiku-1 required_field/3), event_data and type_name (opus-1).

Probe of 22 payloads, run in the scratch folder against each compiled file: in all five, an unknown type gives an unsupported-event error, a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, a string amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}, refunds without payment_id or refund_id name that field, an out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}, and missing or non-map data gives {:missing_field, "data"} or {:invalid_field, "data"}. Differences: a missing "type" gives :invalid_payload in haiku-2 and {:missing_field, "type"} in the others; "type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123} in haiku-2 (event_kind/1's catch-all receives non-strings) and {:invalid_field, "type"} in the others; a present nil amount is reported as missing by opus-1 (as its ParseError @moduledoc says) and invalid by the other four; a negative amount is accepted by haiku-2 only; opus-1 accepts a missing customer_email (optional by design); sonnet-1 rejects payment.failed with failure_reason nil as {:invalid_field, "failure_reason"}, which the prompt's example payload shape allows; a non-map payload raises FunctionClauseError in opus-1 and returns {:error, :invalid_payload} in the others; an unknown type with no data gives unsupported_event in opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2, which check the type first, and {:missing_field, "data"} in haiku-1 and sonnet-1.
